newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Olsten hit after Manpower slide.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Olsten hit after Manpower slide.

text.p: Temporary personnel supplier Olsten Corp shares came under siege Wednesday a day after Manpower Inc, the world's largest private employment agency, broke support.
"When Manpower broke down yesterday, that probably set the tone of things to come for the group. ... What's bad for the goose is bad for the gander," said Lehman Brothers technician Stephen Shobin.
Olsten was the second-most active NYSE issue near midday, off 3-1/8 to 23-1/2 after hitting a year low of 21-5/8.

Manpower slipped 1/4 to 30-1/8 after shedding 4-1/8 Tuesday and falling under support at 30. The stock's decline came after the company guided down analysts' 1996 earnings estimates by a nickel to $1.80 a share.
Ken Tower, a technical analyst at UST Securities, said both stocks "peaked out some months ago and are testing important support zones."

Among stocks in the group, he was most worried about AccuStaff Inc, off 1-1/8 to 24-3/8. Tower said AccuStaff had a neutral trend, but the stock has enjoyed a "nice run" since early 1995 and now has a P/E ratio of 82.
He is "not really negative on the group" but noted Manpower's stock activity put other issues "under a cloud."
Tower said Kelly Services Inc, off 1/16 to 28-7/8, had a P/E ratio of 15-1/2 and "the stock hasn't gone anywhere for years."
He noted Olsten had a 18 P/E, compared with Robert Half International Inc's P/E of 46. Robert Half was off 1-1/2 to 36-1/2.
William Raftery, technical analyst at Smith Barney, voiced some concerns about the near-term outlook on Robert Half. "This stock has had a nice run from 10 in early June 1995."
Some recent IPOs in the group have also enjoyed some nice runs of some 30 percent. RemedyTemp Inc lost 7/8 to 19 and Source Services Corp lost 3/8 to 17-1/4.
